Abscond

/ab-SKOND/ - rhymes with beyond · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Abscond means to sneak away secretly, often taking something along.

The apprentice absconded before dawn with the master glassblower's pattern book, leaving his tools and half a year's wages behind.

Worked Example

For six seasons the touring company trusted its advance agent to carry the box-office takings between towns; in Dover he absconded with the strongbox, having quietly bought a steamer passage under another name.

Abscond is more exact than 'run away' or 'flee' because it adds secrecy and usually something carried off — a person absconds quietly, often with money or goods not their own, and typically to dodge arrest or a debt.

How Abscond Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

flee

flee: to run from danger or pursuit, openly or not

decamp

decamp: to pack up and clear out suddenly — without the stolen goods

Antonyms

surrender

surrender: to hand yourself over instead of running

remain

remain: to stay and face what is coming

How Strong Is It? — depart → abscond → vanish

depart vs. abscond

depart vs. abscond: Depart is perfectly neutral — a train departs on schedule; depart stops far short of abscond, which slips away in secret with something it should not have.

vanish vs. abscond

vanish vs. abscond: Vanish goes further than abscond: the absconder is somewhere down the road with the cash box and a guilty conscience, while a person who vanishes leaves no trail at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — abs-

Prefix — abs-: away

Root — cond

Root — cond: to hide, to stow

Put it together

Put it together: Abs- (away) + cond (to hide, stow) = to stow yourself away. Latin abscondere meant 'to hide well, to bury out of sight'; English kept the sneak-away sense — the absconder hides himself, and usually the takings too.

Use the root in a new word: recondite

Use the root in a new word: recondite: Her thesis wandered into recondite corners of maritime law that even the judges had to look up.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / journalistic

Abscond is the auditor's and the reporter's verb — treasurers abscond with funds, clerks abscond with the till. In casual talk 'ran off with' does the same work; choose abscond when you want the guilty stealth on the record, and note how naturally it pairs with 'with.'
